title: The Law of Life
focus: accepting one's place in nature's cycle

teacherSummary.text: Old Koskoosh, blind and frail, is left by his tribe beside a small fire with a pile of sticks as they move camp in the Arctic winter, as custom requires. He remembers the old moose he once watched wolves bring down and accepts that nature cares only for the race, not the individual. When his fire dies, wolves close in; he lets the firebrand fall.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Old Koskoosh listened greedily” slowly and put it in my own words: Old, blind Koskoosh listens hard to every sound of the camp as it packs up to leave him. Next, craft. I notice the word "greedily," normally used for food, used here for sound. The strongest word is “greedily”: it shows he is hungry for the last signs of his people because hearing is all he has left. Then, effect. Why does Koskoosh listen so greedily? My answer: Koskoosh listens so greedily because hearing is the last tie he has to his departing tribe and to life; the line shows his loneliness and fear as he is left behind to die.
